definition: Invalidate means to make something no longer legally or officially valid or binding, often because of a flaw or technicality rather than a deliberate act.
task: Write one sentence of your own using the word invalidate. Make the sentence show what the word means -- a reader who did not know invalidate should be able to work it out from your sentence.
avoid_verbatim: A single missing signature on the final page was enough to invalidate the entire insurance claim.
Undermine is weaker than invalidate: undermining a contract merely weakens confidence in it, while invalidating it makes it legally void.
Annul is stronger than invalidate: an annulled agreement is wiped away as if it had never existed at all.

To void a document is to cancel it so it has no legal force — a judge voids a fraudulent deed and strikes it down. Invalidate points at the cause as much as the result: a flaw, error, or technicality makes the thing no longer valid, often all by itself. A ruling voids; a missing signature invalidates.

Nullify means to make something count for nothing — a referee nullifies a goal, a court nullifies a result, erasing its effect. Invalidate is the word for documents and claims that lose their legal validity, often through a flaw or technicality. Nullify cancels the effect of a thing; invalidate strips the thing itself of legal standing.

Invalidate means to make something no longer legally or officially valid or binding, often because of a flaw or technicality rather than a deliberate act.
Priya spent months negotiating the sale of her family's bakery.
On signing day, her lawyer noticed that the notary had stamped the wrong page of the contract.
That single clerical error was enough to invalidate the whole agreement, and the sale could not close until a corrected contract was drawn up.
Nobody had acted in bad faith; a technical flaw alone had made the document legally worthless.
The contract became legally void because of a technical flaw, not as a punishment, which is exactly the situation invalidate describes.
formal, legal and technical register
Invalidate usually happens because of a flaw, error, or technicality; nobody has to intend it as a punishment.
Compare rescind, which is a deliberate, formal cancellation of a law, order, or agreement by a governing body, while invalidate describes something becoming legally void, often on its own.

In 1901 the city held a competition for its new library, promising the commission to whichever architect submitted the best design under the contest's strict rules.
The winning drawings were dazzling: a glass-roofed reading room, twin staircases, a hall flooded with northern light.
Then a rival noticed the fine print.
Entries were limited to ten drawings, and the winner had submitted twelve.
The rule violation was enough to invalidate the winning entry on its own; the committee never debated the design's merits, because after the discovery there was nothing left to debate.
The commission passed to the runner-up, and the glass-roofed reading room survives only in a museum archive.
